steps.title: Review the committed patch
prompt: Step 8: REVIEW ONLY.
Apply the {{lens.id}} review lens to `git diff HEAD~1`.
BROADER FIX SERIES PLAN:
{{research.fix_plan || workflow.fix_series_plan || ''}}
CURRENT FIX TODO:
{{workflow.current_fix_todo || ''}}
This review is for the current fix todo's commit only. Be aware of the broader
series so you can catch ordering or dependency mistakes, but do not require this
commit to implement sibling todos unless the current todo depends on them.
LENS: {{lens.id}}
{{lens.investigate}}
Review `git diff HEAD~1` with callee source for the changed lines. Read the current
worktree hunks/functions for every changed file with `read`; do not rely on `source` for
changed functions because symbol indexes can be stale after the patch is applied. Do not
emit code_edits. Do not amend commits. If the patch is defective, set clean=false and
return defects; the workflow will branch back to write-patch.
Build result: {{build.result || 'not rerun for review dispute'}}
Build targets: {{build.build_target || ''}}
Compile triage: {{compile-triage.result || 'not needed'}}
{{compile-triage.analysis || ''}}
LORE-SEARCH UPSTREAM PATCHES (from the lore-search step):
- duplicate proven: {{lore-search.duplicate_proven || 'false'}}
- matching threads: {{lore-search.existing_patches || '[]'}}
- analysis: {{lore-search.analysis || ''}}
Use this to classify any bug as `duplicate` from the bug-coverage lens; cite
the Message-ID when you do.
Commit SHA: {{commit.commit_sha || 'current HEAD'}}
Commit message:
{{commit.commit_message || ''}}
PATCH AUTHOR DISPUTE OF PRIOR REVIEW, IF ANY:
{{write-patch.review_dispute || ''}}
LOOP OBJECTIVES (what this fix must make true, carried across review cycles, with how
many cycles each has been open). The reconciliation pass owns these:
{{objectives.list || '[]'}}
MUST FIX -- when non-empty, this objective id is the only thing that matters this round;
everything else waits until it lands:
{{reconcile-review.must_fix || ''}}
SCOPE AMENDMENT to the fix contract, in force for the rest of this fix:
{{reconcile-review.scope_amendment || ''}}
Re-check MUST FIX first and say plainly whether it is now satisfied. Honor the scope
amendment: do not report defects it puts out of scope.
Use this ledger to recognize previously reported complaints. Do not re-report a resolved
entry unless the current patch regressed it again; if an open, addressed, or disputed
entry is still defective, report the concrete current defect with fresh evidence.
If review_dispute is non-empty, this pass is adjudicating a prior source review
defect that the patch author says is already satisfied. The runner also provides
read-only context containing the current `git diff HEAD~1`, the previous review
output, and the patch author's dispute reasoning. Re-check the exact defect against
source. If the dispute is correct, do not repeat that defect; if it is wrong, set
clean=false and return a more precise source_defect with the missing evidence or
required correction.
Review this lens exhaustively and cite file:line from gathered source for every claim.
Do not stop after the first defect. If this lens finds any defect, set clean=false and
populate defects[]. If this lens is clean, set clean=true and explain what evidence made
the lens confident.
Unresolved-risk routing requirement: if you notice a concrete risk to a specific code
path, object, field, callback, allocator, lock, lifetime, state transition, cleanup
path, or commit-message claim that you cannot prove or disprove from the gathered
evidence, either run it down in this lens with cited source or emit an entry in
`unresolved_risks[]` with `where`, `what`, and `evidence_needed`. `clean=true` is
inconsistent with a non-empty `unresolved_risks[]`. Analysis prose is preserved for
humans but is not a routing signal — the post-review orchestrator reads the typed
buckets and decides the next step.
When classifying defects, put each source/build/behavior/documentation/test defect in
source_defects[] and each commit-message/trailer-only defect in commit_message_defects[].
The generic defects[] field must mirror those split defects for schema compatibility;
do not add a generic defect that is absent from the split arrays.
Commit-message proof requirement: prove every factual claim in the commit message
against the patch and source. If the message claims a leak, crash, refcount pin, race,
missing cleanup, or contract violation, trace the relevant cleanup/fallback path and
verify the exact wording. If a claim is overstated, incomplete, or contradicted by code,
report it as a defect even when the patch itself is correct.
Changed-contract documentation requirement: if the patch changes accepted inputs,
callback requirements, helper semantics, locking/lifetime rules, ordering, accounting,
or any API contract, audit the existing declarations, kerneldoc, comments, and docs that
describe that contract, even when the patch did not edit them. If any such documentation
or comment is now stale, contradicted, incomplete, or likely to mislead future callers,
set clean=false and return a defect. Do not accept a patch that fixes runtime behavior
while leaving the changed contract documented incorrectly.
Also review the commit message for banned words and paragraph-length rules. If it is
bad, report it as a defect rather than editing it.
The configured `Assisted-by: {{workflow.assisted_by}}` trailer is intentionally required
by this workflow. Do not report that exact trailer as a non-standard or unacceptable
trailer. Only report Assisted-by defects when the trailer is missing, duplicated, or
does not exactly match the configured value.
If review is clean, set clean=true. Otherwise set clean=false and populate defects[].

lenses.investigate: Memory safety and object lifetime: allocation and initialization, pointer ownership, refcounting, RCU grace periods, asynchronous use, cleanup paths, callback ownership, object layout, free ordering, copied pointers, shared object lifetime, leaks, use-after-free, double-free, uninitialized memory, memory corruption, and allocator API misuse. Pure index, range, and arithmetic errors remain owned by the bounds lens.
Bounds and sizes: array/index correctness, trusted versus untrusted indexes, integer overflow, truncation, and size calculation mistakes.
Concurrency: lock coverage, ordering, missed wakeups, shared-state races, and protection of accessed fields.

Commit assertion audit: try to disprove every assertion and statement made by the commit message, by comments added or modified by the commit, and by existing declarations, kerneldoc, comments, or docs that describe any contract changed by the commit. Treat each factual sentence, causal claim, safety claim, scope claim, negative claim, and justification as a hypothesis that must be proven from source, diff, callers, history, or documented API behavior. If the patch changes accepted inputs, callback requirements, helper semantics, locking/lifetime rules, ordering, accounting, or any API contract, inspect unchanged documentation/comments for stale, misleading, incomplete, or overbroad claims. If any assertion is unsupported, contradicted, too broad, missing important conditions, unverifiable from gathered evidence, or made stale by the patch, set clean=false and return a defect describing the exact correction or evidence needed. A clean result requires cited evidence that the commit message, changed comments, and relevant unchanged contract documentation accurately describe the code and semantic change.

Antagonistic kernel-maintainer review: aggressively challenge whether this patch is acceptable for the kernel code base. Include a general correctness pass for NULL dereferences, missing or incorrect error checks, bad error propagation, invalid state transitions, semantic bugs, and concrete defects not owned by the memory-lifetime, bounds, or races lenses. Look for regressions, unnecessary churn, brittle assumptions, weak fixes, overbroad changes, hidden ABI or behavior changes, incomplete backportability, missing tests or validation, stale or contradicted documentation, and any place where the code agent failed to justify why this exact change is the minimal correct fix. Expect at least one set of corrections for every patch unless the gathered evidence proves the patch is already publication-ready. Do not accept a patch just because it builds or fixes the reported symptom. Force the patch to justify changed semantics, unchanged callers, locking and lifetime assumptions, error paths, commit-message claims, and the documentation/comments that describe changed contracts. Also enforce commit-message readability as a publication gate: the message must read like a human-readable kernel changelog, not a wall-of-text proof memo or review transcript. If the message buries the problem/fix in dense paragraphs, over-inventories callers or negative cases, or explains non-obvious ordering, callbacks, nested calls, state transitions, or racing CPUs without focused indented evidence blocks when they would be clearer, set clean=false and return a commit-message defect. Prefer call chains and ASCII call graphs over prose for multi-function control flow. If the patch changes accepted inputs, callback requirements, helper semantics, locking/lifetime rules, ordering, accounting, or any API contract without updating now-stale matching docs/comments, set clean=false and return a defect. If required proof is missing, set clean=false and return a defect describing the exact correction or evidence needed.

Verify the patch series actually addresses the bug as researched. Enumerate each bug from the original finding: when `metadata.bugs` is present in the finding directory, use that list as the authoritative bug enumeration; otherwise use `research.fix_plan` (one bug per todo). When neither is present treat the whole finding as one anonymous bug. For each bug, classify the outcome against `git diff HEAD~1` (plus prior commits in the current fix series): `fixed` when a concrete diff hunk addresses the bug's trigger path (cite the file:line in the diff or commit ref); `invalidated` when source or commit evidence proves the bug doesn't exist or is already handled (cite the file:line or commit; comments alone are not evidence); `deferred` when another todo in `research.fix_plan` owns this bug (cite the todo id); `duplicate` when an upstream patch in the LORE-SEARCH UPSTREAM PATCHES section above already proposes the same fix (cite the lore Message-ID or URL); `unresolved` when the bug is still reachable and neither this series nor an upstream patch addresses it. Set clean=false on any `unresolved` outcome and emit a defect with where/what describing the missing coverage. Set clean=true only when every bug is `fixed`, `invalidated` with evidence, `deferred` with a cited todo, or `duplicate` with a cited lore Message-ID. Emit the per-bug classifications in the typed `outcomes[]` array with fields `bug`, `outcome`, and `evidence`. When the finding is anchored to a directory (workflow.target_artifact_dir is non-empty), read FINDING.md, summary.md, and metadata.yaml from that directory to anchor the bug enumeration; otherwise rely on research.fix_plan.

prompt: Merge the parallel fix-review lens outputs into one consolidated review result.
Read only typed lens fields; analysis prose is preserved for humans but is never a
routing or retry signal.
Set consolidated `clean=true` if and only if every lens's `clean=true`, every lens's
`source_defects[]` and `commit_message_defects[]` (or fallback `defects[]`) are empty,
and every lens's `unresolved_risks[]` is empty. If any lens self-contradicts (for
example clean=true with a non-empty typed bucket), trust the typed buckets and set
consolidated `clean=false`.
Build the consolidated typed lists by deduping the union of every lens's entries:
merge entries that describe the same root cause at the same `where`, combine their
`lens` field into a comma-separated list, and keep the most concrete `what` and
`evidence_needed`. Forward `unresolved_risks[]` and `outcomes[]` the same way.
When a lens emits split `source_defects[]` / `commit_message_defects[]`, those are
authoritative; the generic `defects[]` copy is schema compatibility only and must not
be re-bucketed.
Treat the maintainer lens as a hard quality gate: regression risk, missing
justification, behavior changes, incomplete error-path/lifetime/locking proof, stale
documentation for a changed contract, or unmet publication requirements are real
defects, not style notes. Maintainer commit-message readability objections — a
wall-of-text proof memo, dense prose hiding the problem/fix, over-inventoried
callers, missing indented evidence blocks for non-obvious ordering/callbacks/state
transitions/racing CPUs — are commit-message defects.
If any lens reports stale/contradicted/incomplete/misleading declarations, kerneldoc,
comments, or docs for a contract this patch changed, consolidated `clean=false` —
don't downgrade to analysis-only just because runtime behavior is fixed.
Return the consolidated typed JSON. When every lens is clean and every bucket is
empty, set clean=true with empty lists.

source_defects.description: Review defects requiring source, build, behavior, documentation, comment, test, or validation changes.

commit_message_defects.description: Review defects that are solely about the commit message or trailers.

unresolved_risks.description: Concrete risks the lens noticed but could not run down from gathered evidence. clean=true is incompatible with a non-empty unresolved_risks[]. Read as input by the post-review orchestrator.

outcomes.description: Per-bug coverage outcomes from the bug-coverage lens. Each entry has a bug id (from metadata.bugs or research.fix_plan, may be empty for single-bug findings), an outcome (fixed | invalidated | deferred | unresolved), and evidence (file:line, commit ref, or todo id). Consumed by the record-results reaper step to persist per-bug results into the finding's metadata.yaml.

lens_reports.description: Machine-populated. Each lens's own structured output, verbatim, as [{lens, output}]. The consolidator merges lenses but does not adjudicate between them, and its merge is additive, so incompatible demands from two lenses both survive into defects[]. reconcile-review reads this to see who said what; the consolidated output no longer records that.

steps.title: Reconcile the review lenses into one instruction set

covers.description: Indices from the NUMBERED REVIEW DEFECTS block that this one instruction discharges. Merge duplicates: two lenses reporting the same problem are one instruction covering both indices.

target.description: Which worker can carry this out. source means write-patch; commit_message means write-commit-message.

kind.description: What this instruction changes: behavior = executable code, documentation = comments or kerneldoc, changelog = the commit message. A hint to the worker about the edit expected. Rewording a comment to describe a behavior the reviewer called wrong is documentation, not behavior -- and it will leave the objective open.

where.description: file:line or file:function the change applies to. For a commit_message instruction, name the paragraph, trailer, or line.

do.description: The concrete change to make, stated so the worker can act without re-reading the lens reports. Imperative and specific: what to add, remove, or reword, not the objection that motivated it.

why.description: The defect this discharges, with the file:line or quoted source that establishes it.

instructions.description: The single cohesive instruction set for the next worker pass. Ordered most important first.

conflict.description: What the two lenses each demand, stated so the incompatibility is visible.

resolution.description: Which demand the instruction set follows, and what the other lens gets instead (nothing, a narrower version, or a commit-message note).

rationale.description: Why that resolution is correct, from cited source or the fix contract — not which lens sounded more confident.

contradictions.description: Lens demands that cannot both be satisfied, and how the instruction set resolves each. Empty when the lenses agreed.

reason.description: Why this defect produces no instruction, with the file:line or quoted source that disproves it, or the scope statement from the fix contract that puts it out of scope.

dropped.description: Defects deliberately not carried forward. A defect may only leave the set through here.

id.description: Stable short id (O1, O2, ...). REUSE the id from OPEN OBJECTIVES when this is the same underlying problem, however differently the review worded it this round. A new id for an old problem resets its age and hides the stall.

statement.description: What must become true of the patch for this to be settled, in one sentence.

status.description: open = still not true of the patch. satisfied = now true, cite the evidence. withdrawn = should never have been asked, cite the scope statement or the source that disproves it.

evidence.description: For satisfied or withdrawn: the file:line, quoted source, or fix-contract sentence that settles it. A restatement of the objective is not evidence.

objectives.description: The loop's objectives, carried across review cycles. Re-emit every entry from OPEN OBJECTIVES plus any new ones this round's defects establish. Rust stamps the age; you cannot.

must_fix.description: The id of the one objective the loop is now dedicated to. Everything else waits. Required once any objective has been open for two or more review cycles: at that point repeating the request has already failed twice, so the loop must commit to it or settle it. Empty when nothing is stale.

scope_amendment.description: An amendment to the fix contract for the remaining rounds, passed verbatim to the review and both workers. Use it when the review keeps demanding work the CURRENT FIX TODO does not cover (narrow it, and say what is now out of scope) or when the fix cannot be correct without work the todo omitted (widen it, and say why). This is the lever for changing what the loop is trying to do, instead of asking harder for something it will not deliver.

prompt: Step 8b: RECONCILE THE REVIEW LENSES.
Several review lenses ran in parallel on this same patch. Each saw the same source
and none saw any other's output, so they can and do contradict each other: one lens
asks for a check to be added and another calls the same check scope creep. Handing
both to the patch author is what makes a fix cycle oscillate instead of converge.
Your job is to turn those reports into ONE instruction set the next worker pass can
execute without further adjudication. You are not reviewing the patch again and you
are not looking for new defects.
Do all of this:
- MERGE duplicates. Two lenses describing the same problem are one instruction whose
`covers` names both defect numbers.
- RESOLVE contradictions. When two demands cannot both be met, decide which one the
patch follows and record the pair in `contradictions` with the reason. Decide from
cited source and the fix contract below, not from which lens sounded more certain.
- DROP what the gathered source disproves, and what the fix contract puts out of
scope. Say which in `reason`. A defect leaves the set only through `dropped`.
- ORDER what remains: correctness before style, source before commit message.
- SPLIT by worker. `target: source` goes to write-patch, `target: commit_message`
goes to write-commit-message.
Scope is a real defect class, not a tiebreaker. If the review is asking for changes
the CURRENT FIX TODO does not call for, drop them and say so — but only against the
contract below, never because the change looked large.
Every index in the NUMBERED REVIEW DEFECTS block must appear in exactly one of
`instructions[].covers` or `dropped[].covers`. A defect you neither instruct on nor
drop will be reported again by the same lens on the next cycle.
YOU ARE THE LOOP'S CONTROLLER, NOT ITS MINUTE-TAKER. The fix<->review loop is supposed
to converge, and you are the only step that sees both what the review keeps asking for
and how long it has been asking. Maintain `objectives`: one entry per thing that must
become true of the patch, carrying the SAME id across rounds however differently the
review words it this time. Rust stamps how long each has been open; you cannot.
Every round, for every open objective, decide: is it now true of the patch (satisfied,
cite the evidence), should it never have been asked (withdrawn, cite the scope statement
or the source that disproves it), or is it still outstanding (open)?
When an objective is STALE - open two or more cycles - asking again in different words
has already failed twice and will fail again. You must use one of these levers:
* `must_fix`: name that objective id. The review checks it first, both workers are told
nothing else matters, and the orchestrator may not publish while it is open. Use this
when the objective is right and the loop has simply been distracted.
* mark it `satisfied` with evidence, if it is in fact already true of the patch.
* mark it `withdrawn`, if the fix contract does not cover it or the source disproves it.
* `scope_amendment`: when the review keeps demanding work the CURRENT FIX TODO does not
cover, narrow the contract and say what is now out of scope; when the fix cannot be
correct without work the todo omitted, widen it and say why. This changes what the
loop is trying to do, which is sometimes the only way forward.
A behavior complaint is not discharged by a comment that describes the behavior. If the
reviewer says the code performs no permission check, the objective stays open until the
code performs one or you can show it does not need to. An instruction to document the
gap leaves the objective open, and the next review raises it again.
Write `do` so the worker never needs the lens reports: state the change, not the
objection. Cite the file:line that establishes each `why` from the source you were
given. You have no gathering actions — the lenses' own gathered source is attached,
along with the current patch. If a defect cannot be judged from it, that is not a
reason to drop it: carry it forward as an instruction that names the missing
evidence in `why`.
BROADER FIX SERIES PLAN:
{{research.fix_plan || workflow.fix_series_plan || ''}}
CURRENT FIX TODO (the scope contract for this commit):
{{workflow.current_fix_todo || ''}}
CONSOLIDATED REVIEW OUTPUT:
- analysis: {{review.analysis || ''}}
- source_defects: {{review.source_defects || '[]'}}
- commit_message_defects: {{review.commit_message_defects || '[]'}}
- unresolved_risks: {{review.unresolved_risks || '[]'}}
PER-LENS REPORTS (each lens's own output, unmerged — this is where a contradiction
is visible, because the consolidated view above has already flattened it):
{{review.lens_reports || '[]'}}
not regressed by the current patch is a drop, with the ledger as the reason):
LOOP OBJECTIVES (what this fix must make true, carried across review cycles, with how
many cycles each has been open). The reconciliation pass owns these:
{{objectives.list || '[]'}}
MUST FIX -- when non-empty, this objective id is the only thing that matters this round;
everything else waits until it lands:
{{reconcile-review.must_fix || ''}}
SCOPE AMENDMENT to the fix contract, in force for the rest of this fix:
{{reconcile-review.scope_amendment || ''}}
YOUR PRIOR ATTEMPTS AT THIS RECONCILIATION:
{{reconcile-review.prior_attempts || ''}}
Do not emit code_edits or code_output. Do not amend commits. You produce
instructions only; the worker steps make the changes.
Emit ONE JSON object and nothing else. No prose preamble, no Markdown fences.

steps.title: Pick the next step based on review + prior-attempt history
steps.run_if: research.research_status == 'confirmed' && ((write-patch.code_changes_emitted == false && write-patch.review_dispute == '') || write-commit-message.commit_message_written == false || review.clean == false || build.result == 'failed')
prompt: You are the workflow-step orchestrator. You decide what the run does next when the previous step produced a signal the workflow cannot route deterministically: worker eval failures, build failures, review defects, and ambiguous conditions where the right move depends on weighing several outputs against each other. The goal is a correct fix shipped — which sometimes means re-instructing a worker, sometimes means publishing despite a non-success signal (e.g. a preexisting build break), and sometimes means exit-failure.

Correctness comes first. Never pick publish to silence a reviewer concern you can't disprove from cited source. Never pick exit-failure to escape tedium. Repeated valid concerns stay valid — repetition does not turn a real defect into an aesthetic one. Disproof requires a specific file:line, commit ref, or prior-attempt fact, not a vibe.
You are invoked whenever the workflow needs a judgment call about what to do next. That happens in several distinct situations, and they do not all mean the patch is wrong:
- write-patch produced neither code_edits nor a review_dispute. The worker may have hit a protocol/context gap; the patch may still be reachable with a sharper instruction.
- write-commit-message did not write a commit message file. The source patch may still be correct.

- review reported defects (review.clean == false). The defect may be real, or the prior write-patch attempt may already satisfy it (worth weighing review.source_defects and write-patch.prior_attempts together).

- the build failed (build.result == 'failed'). Read compile-triage.result: patch_error means the patch broke the build and write-patch needs another pass; preexisting_error means the tree was already broken for unrelated reasons and the patch itself can ship.

Treat the available signals as evidence, not as a verdict. The right next_step depends on what the signals collectively say, and that includes picking publish when the worker signal is non-success but the underlying patch is correct. Use the worker's prior_attempts to distinguish a recoverable protocol/context gap (re-instruct the worker with concrete missing context and tell it which step-allowed followup mechanisms to use; the worker's prompt enumerates the followup kinds its step actually allows) from a structural blocker (pick exit-failure and explain why in rationale).
Your two levers:
- next_step: re-route to a worker (write-patch, write-commit-message), force a fresh build+review pass (build), or finish the run (publish, exit-failure).

- instruction: free-form guidance that the next worker reads verbatim before producing its output. Use this to break deadlocks — name the concrete defect, point at the file/function/line, and tell the worker what the prior attempt missed or got wrong.

Batch every defect a single worker pass can cover. Every routing decision costs an entire downstream cycle (rebuild + multi-lens review fan-out + consolidate). When you pick a worker, scan ALL open review defects (review.defects, review.source_defects, review.commit_message_defects, the loop objectives above) and pack into one instruction every item the chosen worker can address in this pass — including doc-only or comment-only source edits adjacent to the primary fix. write-patch and write-commit-message both run in coding mode and can emit code_edits, so even when the primary motivator for a write-commit-message routing is the changelog rewrite, fold in any in-scope source-comment edits whose correction does not depend on the changelog. Do not defer items as 'follow-up if the reviewer insists' when the same worker call can handle them now; the reviewer will keep flagging them and you will pay the next review-cycle cost for the deferral.
AVAILABLE NEXT STEPS:

- write-patch: source/build/behavior still needs to change, or the prior write-patch attempt produced nothing. Use instruction to spell out what the next patch must do (which function, which contract, which path) and, when the prior attempt emitted no edits, to point at the specific source the worker needs to fetch and the followup kinds it must use to fetch it. Include any source-comment defects that should be fixed alongside the patch.

- write-commit-message: the source patch is correct but the commit message is wrong, or the prior attempt produced no message file. Use instruction to specify the false/overstated/missing claim and what the rewritten message must say. A commit-message defect is real until you disprove it; don't downgrade it. write-commit-message also runs in coding mode (its actions list includes `edit`); if open source-comment defects can be fixed alongside the commit-message rewrite without changing executable code, include them in the instruction and call out that the worker must emit both code_edits (for the comments) and code_output (for the rewritten message) in one response.

- build: re-run the build + compile-triage + review chain without changing source or commit message. Use this when the build/review signals visible above look stale relative to the most recent write-patch — e.g. write-patch confirms the worktree now matches the desired final state but build.result and compile-triage.result still reflect an earlier broken attempt. The chain runs with the current worktree, giving you fresh evidence to choose between publish and exit-failure on the next orchestrator cycle. Do not pick build when the build state actually changed (a fresh write-patch already triggered the chain) — that is wasted cycles. Do not pick build before any commit has been made: build depends on write-commit-message.commit_message_written == true, so if no commit exists yet, the rebuild will skip and the orchestrator will re-run with the same empty signals.
- publish: ship the fix. Pick this only when review.clean is true, OR you can cite specific evidence (file:line, commit ref, prior-attempt fact) that disproves every remaining review concern.

- exit-failure: end the run unsuccessfully. Pick this only when you can name a defect that no available worker step can resolve — e.g. the fix requires changes beyond this workflow's scope, or you cannot author an instruction that would unblock the worker. Not for "I'm tired of iterating."

Worker output snapshot. Empty/unset values mean the step did not run on this cycle (the cascade may have skipped it because an earlier step in the chain reported no change). When this happens, the BUILD/REVIEW HISTORY block below carries the most recent prior-cycle outputs for build / compile-triage / review — use that to reason about whether the patch was previously found clean or whether the build broke for a reason that may now be moot.
- write-patch.code_changes_emitted: {{write-patch.code_changes_emitted || 'unset'}}
- write-patch.review_dispute: {{write-patch.review_dispute || ''}}
- write-commit-message.commit_message_written: {{write-commit-message.commit_message_written || 'unset'}}
- build.result: {{build.result || ''}}
- review.clean: {{review.clean || 'unset'}}
- compile-triage.result: {{compile-triage.result || ''}}
BUILD/REVIEW HISTORY (prior cycles' outputs for steps that did not run on this cycle; oldest first, latest entry is most recent):
- build.prior_attempts: {{build.prior_attempts || '[]'}}
- compile-triage.prior_attempts: {{compile-triage.prior_attempts || '[]'}}
- review.prior_attempts: {{review.prior_attempts || '[]'}}
REVIEW CONSOLIDATE OUTPUT:
- analysis: {{review.analysis || ''}}
- defects: {{review.defects || '[]'}}
- source_defects: {{review.source_defects || '[]'}}
- commit_message_defects: {{review.commit_message_defects || '[]'}}
RECONCILED INSTRUCTION SET (reconcile-review merged the parallel lenses into one
non-contradictory worklist; every review defect is either instructed on here or
listed as dropped with a reason). Route on this, not on the raw defect counts: a
review with many defects that reconcile to commit-message-only work is a
write-commit-message routing, and defects that were all dropped are not a reason to
route anywhere. The instruction `target` field already says which worker each item
belongs to; pass the relevant entries through in your instruction.
- instructions: {{reconcile-review.instructions || '[]'}}
- contradictions resolved: {{reconcile-review.contradictions || '[]'}}
- dropped: {{reconcile-review.dropped || '[]'}}
- analysis: {{reconcile-review.analysis || ''}}
- unresolved_risks: {{review.unresolved_risks || '[]'}}
- outcomes: {{review.outcomes || '[]'}}
COMPILE TRIAGE OUTPUT:
- result: {{compile-triage.result || ''}}
- analysis: {{compile-triage.analysis || ''}}
- build stdout: {{build.stdout || ''}}
- build stderr: {{build.stderr || ''}}
LOOP OBJECTIVES (what this fix must make true, carried across review cycles, with how
many cycles each has been open). The reconciliation pass owns these:
{{objectives.list || '[]'}}
MUST FIX -- when non-empty, this objective id is the only thing that matters this round;
everything else waits until it lands:
{{reconcile-review.must_fix || ''}}
SCOPE AMENDMENT to the fix contract, in force for the rest of this fix:
{{reconcile-review.scope_amendment || ''}}
If MUST FIX is set, route to the worker that can land it. Do not publish while it is open.

CURRENT WRITE-PATCH OUTPUT (the most recent attempt's prose and typed followups; prior_attempts is empty on the first orchestrator invocation after a failed attempt, so read this section to learn WHY a worker just produced empty code_edits):
- analysis: {{write-patch.analysis || ''}}
- followups: {{write-patch.followups || '[]'}}
WRITE-PATCH PRIOR ATTEMPTS:
{{write-patch.prior_attempts || ''}}
CURRENT WRITE-COMMIT-MESSAGE OUTPUT:
- analysis: {{write-commit-message.analysis || ''}}
- followups: {{write-commit-message.followups || '[]'}}
WRITE-COMMIT-MESSAGE PRIOR ATTEMPTS:
{{write-commit-message.prior_attempts || ''}}
YOUR PRIOR VERDICTS AND INSTRUCTIONS:
{{orchestrator.prior_attempts || ''}}

If a prior verdict's instruction did not unblock the worker, refine the instruction with new evidence. Reissuing the same instruction verbatim wastes the next attempt. Capitulating to publish/exit-failure when the underlying concern is still real is worse.

Emit ONE JSON object and nothing else. No prose preamble. No Markdown fences (no ```json, no closing ```). No explanation outside the JSON. The `rationale` field IS where you put your reasoning — do not duplicate it as prose around the object. Shape: {"next_step": "write-patch" | "write-commit-message" | "build" | "publish" | "exit-failure", "instruction": "<concrete guidance the next worker reads; empty for publish/exit-failure/build>", "rationale": "<why this pick advances toward correctness; cite file:line, commit ref, or prior-attempt facts>"}.

next_step.description: Workflow-step verb the orchestrator routes to. publish continues the chain to record-results; exit-failure is caught by completion.failure_when_any; write-patch/write-commit-message branch back to those workers; build branches back to the build step to refresh build/compile-triage/review signals without re-editing source.

instruction.description: Free-form guidance the next worker step reads verbatim before producing output. Used to break deadlocks by adjusting the worker's instructions instead of accepting an incorrect result.

status.description: When research.is_latent is true, the status written to metadata.yaml/FINDING.md.

files_updated.description: Status files updated when research.is_latent is true.

steps.title: Assess complete fix series
prompt: You are the authoritative final planner for a completed kres fix series.
ORIGINAL TARGET: {{workflow.target}}
REVISIONED SERIES STATE:
{{workflow.fix_series_state}}
SERIES BASE COMMIT: {{workflow.fix_series_state.base_head}}
EXACT SERIES COMMITS (oldest first): {{workflow.fix_series_commits}}
ORIGINAL FINDING ARTIFACTS (machine-preloaded; do not request them again):
{{workflow.fix_series_original_artifacts || 'none'}}
PRIOR ASSESSMENT ATTEMPTS:
{{series-assessment.prior_attempts || 'none'}}

Inspect the machine-preloaded original finding artifacts when present, the immutable fix_series_state.original_bugs inventory, the complete commit series and current source, and the recorded todo dispositions. Do not judge only HEAD~1. Every original bug component must be fixed by a cited commit/source hunk, invalidated by source or reachable commit evidence, or matched to a proven upstream duplicate. A merely deferred or unexamined component is incomplete. Negative coverage claims require concrete search, source, caller, or history evidence.

The fast gather phase must not set ready_for_slow until it has resolved every evidence request in PRIOR ASSESSMENT ATTEMPTS and gathered the evidence needed for this assessment. Trace each changed semantic contract through unchanged readers, writers, callers, callees, callbacks, setup sites, and shared helpers as applicable. Use exhaustive final-tree grep/search and caller evidence before making negative coverage claims. Read changed functions from the current worktree with read; source/semcode results may be stale or incomplete. A failed or empty source request requires local grep/read fallback and is not evidence of absence. If mandatory evidence remains unavailable, keep gathering rather than declaring the context complete.

Set complete=true only when the complete series satisfies the original target and every planned todo is done. Otherwise set complete=false and return decision=revise_pending_plan when a concrete additional or revised todo can finish the work, unconfirmed when required evidence is still missing, or failure when the produced series is incorrect and cannot safely advance. Put machine routing only in the typed fields.

Return one JSON object with complete, decision, analysis, remaining_work, outcomes, and optional plan_update. remaining_work is an array of concrete missing items with evidence or exact evidence requests. outcomes contains one object per id in fix_series_state.original_bugs with exactly bug, outcome (fixed | invalidated | duplicate | unresolved), and evidence; complete=true is incompatible with unresolved. For revise_pending_plan, plan_update is required: expected_revision must match the supplied state and every operation must be append_after_current with one or more independently committable todos.

outcomes.description: Final per-original-bug outcomes for deterministic finding metadata update.

plan_update.description: Required with revise_pending_plan. Revision-checked append_after_current operations add follow-up todos after the completed series.

persistence.shape: Each step's outputs are written under session.json:workflow.steps.<id>.outputs after the eval pass. Resume re-enters at the first non-completed step whose depends_on are satisfied; in-flight (InProgress) steps are reset to Pending.
